answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by making each identity earn non-transferable reputation through verified work over time, like a slow ocean current rather than a sudden zephyr. New identities start with a tiny transaction cap, and only after many completed, audited tasks does that cap rise. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs real time and verifiable effort for each one, while an umber audit trail makes sudden bursts of new accounts easy to spot and throttle before they can drain rewards.
